trade.text: He opposes Trump’s tariffs, saying they raise the cost of groceries and everyday items.
trade.quote: I’m focused on tackling the affordability crisis by standing against Trump’s tariffs that are driving up the cost of groceries and everyday items

debt.text: He says he will oppose cuts to Social Security benefits and increases to the retirement age.
debt.quote: I will oppose efforts to privatize the program, cut benefits, or push the retirement age further out for working families.

housing.text: He supports increasing housing supply and cutting red tape to lower housing costs.
housing.quote: I’ll work to bring down the cost of housing, expand opportunities for first time homebuyers, increase housing supply, cut red tape that drives up costs

schools.text: He says he supports investment in strong public schools.
schools.quote: That means investing in strong public schools, standing up for LGBTQ+ individuals, and protecting the fundamental right to make personal health decisions

immigration.text: He supports expanding legal status, protecting asylum seekers, and creating a pathway to citizenship.
immigration.quote: I support permanently protecting Dreamers, expanding access to legal status, defending asylum protections, and ending policies that criminalize families seeking safety.

guns.text: He supports universal background checks, including for gun-show and private sales.
guns.quote: So I support universal background checks, closing the loopholes for gun shows and private sales, which is what that is.

abortion.text: He supports restoring Roe protections in federal law and says abortion decisions should not be made by politicians.
abortion.quote: I support codifying Roe into federal law to ensure women’s health decisions are protected nationwide.

cannabis.text: He voted for the MORE Act, which would remove marijuana from the federal Controlled Substances Act.
cannabis.quote: Vote Question: On Passage MORE Act Vote Type: Yea-And-Nay Status: Passed

energy.text: He supports curbing greenhouse gas emissions and expanding clean energy.
energy.quote: I will work in Congress to curb greenhouse gas emissions and address the many other environmental crises facing our state

voting.text: He voted for the For the People Act, an election reform bill that included measures to expand voter access.
voting.quote: Vote Question: On Passage For the People Act Vote Type: Yea-And-Nay Status: Passed

tax.text: He proposes ending federal income taxes on individuals over ten years and shifting revenue authority to the states.
tax.quote: End federal income taxation on individual citizens over a locked 10-year horizon, restoring the original constitutional design by shifting revenue authority entirely back to the states.

debt.text: He calls for halting federal money printing as part of his fiscal platform.
debt.quote: Stop Over-Spending: Halt the reckless federal money-printing that drives up the daily cost of gas, groceries, and housing.

housing.text: He proposes legalizing and streamlining missing-middle housing, including duplexes, townhomes, and small apartments.
housing.quote: Legalize and streamline "missing-middle" housing like duplexes, townhomes, and small apartments.

schools.text: He describes support for decentralized education pathways and an open marketplace of school choice; the page does not specify vouchers.
schools.quote: Decentralized educational pathways, absolute parental authority over data exposure, customizable learning tracks, and an open marketplace of competitive school choice without uniform state dictation.

guns.text: He says his plan would protect Second Amendment rights, oppose sweeping restrictions, and focus enforcement on violent offenders and illegal supply chains.
guns.quote: To reduce violence by treating root environmental and psychological causes while completely protecting your Second Amendment rights:

abortion.text: He opposes criminal bans and supports legal protections for emergencies, rape, and incest, while saying his goal is to reduce abortions through support for families.
abortion.quote: Criminalizing abortion does not work to eradicate the practice. To reduce abortion through compassionate, practical support rather than police power, our focus centers on root-cause solutions:

health.text: He proposes a universal catastrophic-care safety net while keeping everyday care open to private competition and restricting some public benefits to lawful residents.
health.quote: Establishing a universal safety net for major medical emergencies while keeping everyday care open to honest, competitive choice, and ensuring baseline public health rules apply uniformly to protect community stability.

tax.text: After the debate, Owen opposed higher taxes and called for market-based incentives and more efficient services.
tax.quote: One of us wanted bigger taxes and more taxation and bigger government, and I want creative solutions, market-based incentives, making services more efficient.

trade.text: He called free trade the best policy but endorsed targeted tariffs to punish bad actors or support domestic industries.
trade.quote: Owen said he believes free trade is the best economic policy, but said tariffs can be a tool used to "punish bad actors" or to incentivize or grow domestic industries.

debt.text: Owen opposed cutting Social Security benefits or raising the retirement age and proposed investing the fund in the stock market.
debt.quote: Owen said he does not support a tax increase, raising the retirement age or cutting benefits to keep the fund solvent.

housing.text: Owen says he would tie federal funding to local zoning reform as a way to support affordable housing.
housing.quote: Riley will fight for affordable housing through conditionalizing federal funding to localities implementing common-sense zoning reform.

schools.text: In a candidate questionnaire, Owen supported investment and funding for school-based mental-health services as part of public education.
schools.quote: One of the most impactful approaches to improving access to mental health services for young people in Utah is investing in school-based mental health support as a foundational component of public education.
